newsitem.title: USA: Defense rests in sentencing part of McVeigh case.
newsitem.headline: Defense rests in sentencing part of McVeigh case.

text.p: The defense rested its case on Wednesday in the sentencing phase of the trial of Timothy McVeigh, convicted of the April 1995 bombing of a federal building in Oklahoma City that killed 168 people.
The last witnesses to testify on McVeigh's behalf were his parents, who pleaded with the jury to spare his life.
Judge Richard Matsch set closing arguments in the sentencing phase of the trial for Thursday morning.
McVeigh, a Gulf War veteran, was convicted on June 2 of bombing the Oklahoma City federal building on April 19, 1995. Inb addition to the 168 people killed, the blast injured more than 500.
The same jury is now to decide whether he will be executed or spend his life in prison.

McVeigh's mother Mildred Frazer pleaded for her son's life, saying "He is a human being just as we all are." His father William McVeigh narrated a videotape made of home movies from McVeigh's childhood.
